items.summary: TwinFix is a new AI agent designed to automate the diagnosis, reproduction, and repair of software bugs within isolated, disposable 'twin' environments. Unlike existing AI SRE tools that focus primarily on diagnosis, TwinFix modifies business code and verifies the fix against hidden tests before submitting it for human approval. The system supports multiple languages including Java, Python, Go, and TypeScript, and integrates with CI/CD pipelines using Docker Compose or Kubernetes. It enforces a strict workflow: diagnosis, reproduction in a twin environment, repair, independent verification, and final human review.

items.title: SGLang RCE Exploit Breaches NEAR AI, Steals Data From 18 Agents and About 100 Users
items.one_liner: A vulnerability in the SGLang inference engine allowed an attacker to breach NEAR AI, exposing user data and AI agent logs.
items.summary: NEAR AI suffered a data breach after an attacker exploited a remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in the SGLang inference engine. The attacker gained access to an internal system, exposing account details for approximately 100 users and sensitive data from 18 AI agents. While the company utilized a trusted execution environment (TEE), the vulnerability existed within the software running inside it, rendering the TEE protection ineffective for this specific attack.
items.bottom_line: The NEAR AI breach demonstrates that trusted execution environments (TEEs) do not protect against vulnerabilities in the software running within them.

items.title: Coding Agent Security for AppSec Leaders: Start With What Agents Can Reach
items.one_liner: Coding agents are a new attack surface; secure them by limiting their access to credentials and sensitive environment variables.
items.summary: AppSec teams must shift focus from code-level vulnerabilities to the broader reach of AI coding agents. These agents often have access to local environment variables, cloud credentials, and internal APIs that can be exploited if the agent is compromised or makes a poor decision. The PocketOS incident, where an agent used a found API token to delete production data, highlights the danger of over-scoped credentials. Security teams are encouraged to implement technical enforcement layers rather than relying solely on written policy.
key_facts: Risk: Over-scoped credentials and environment access
items.bottom_line: Your security strategy for AI agents must prioritize limiting their 'blast radius' by restricting the credentials and system access they can reach, rather than just reviewing their generated code.
